subject: Intermittent outbound connections dropped after SNAT pool update
messages:
From: ops-support@brightline.io
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: network-sre@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-03-22T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Outbound failures to vendor: SYN seen but no SYN-ACK returned to host

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing intermittent failures from Brightline staging nodes to Vendor API (api.vendor.example.com). Symptoms: the staging host sends SYN, vendor replies with SYN-ACK (we can see it on our egress tap), but the SYN-ACK never arrives at the application host. The problem started right after we rotated the SNAT pool during a maintenance change at ~07:45 PT.

What we've captured so far: we ran tcpdump on the staging host and on the egress NAT box (attached pcap-snippet.pcap). On the NAT box the SYN->SYN-ACK flow completes, but the conntrack mapping shows the reverse path using a different SNAT address intermittently (SNAT reallocation). We also observed occasional 1500->900 MSS differences in the path (fragmentation spikes).

Impact: ~2-3% of outbound connections to that vendor fail with a connection timeout, affecting background jobs and user-facing syncs.

Attaching pcap and a snapshot of conntrack/NAT mappings (nat-mapping-snapshot.txt). Can you advise next steps or a short mitigation? We've flagged a support ticket with the vendor and copied their SREs.

Thanks,
Tomek Kowalski
Network Ops — Brightline Health
ops-support@brightline.io

(attachment: pcap-snippet.pcap, nat-mapping-snapshot.txt)

Thanks Tomek — good details and appreciate the pcaps. Putting Karthik on this for NAT/conntrack analysis and Marissa for private-deploy routing/context. A few quick asks so we can triage faster:

- Can you confirm the source IP and ephemeral port from the staging host tcpdump and the corresponding source NAT observed on the egress?
- Do you have the exact timestamp(s) of a failed transaction so we can correlate logs across the Egress LB and infra?
- Is the SNAT rotation deterministic (round-robin) or tied to conntrack hash changes?

Short-term mitigation idea: if this is SNAT reallocation across a multi-node NAT cluster, we can try pinning flows (affinity) or temporarily increasing conntrack timeout to reduce churn. Also MSS/clamp on the firewall if fragments are involved. Please include any vendor logs if available.

I propose a 30m war-room at 09:00 PT if that works for everyone — I’ll drop a calendar invite.

Subject: Re: Outbound failures to vendor: SYN seen but no SYN-ACK returned to host

Folks — quick read of the artifacts:

What I see:
- The conntrack/NAT snapshot shows SNAT mappings being rehashed across the NAT cluster when the ephemeral port space wraps or when the upstream egress node rebalances. That can produce a window where the reverse path is not pinned to the same NAT translation, so the SYN-ACK returns via a different NAT node and the flow is dropped.
- The pcap shows path MTU/fragmentation anomalies — vendor path appears to force an MSS lower than what our internal PMTU probes assume. Some SYNs advertise MSS=1460, others 1360; combined with retranslation this can produce out-of-window packets.

Immediate mitigations to try (ordered):
1) Apply MSS clamp (1360) at the egress firewall/load-balancer to eliminate fragment-related drops.
2) Increase conntrack timeout for SYN-received/established short-lived flows (adjust by 30-60s) to reduce rehash churn.
3) If using a multi-node SNAT (stateless rehash), enable SNAT affinity/pinning for the Brightline staging subnet.

Longer-term: unify SNAT pools per egress node or adopt consistent-hash keyed on 5-tuple so reverse path remains stable across HA events. Also validate PMTU across GRE/VXLAN overlays — we may be seeing 900B MTU slices on the vendor path.

I can prepare iptables/sysctl commands for mitigation if you want me to push them. Recommend war-room now.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attaching checklist and a small pcap snippet that isolates a failing flow.

Subject: Re: Outbound failures to vendor: SYN seen but no SYN-ACK returned to host

Thanks all — following the war-room we applied the MSS clamp and increased conntrack timeout; we also enabled SNAT affinity for the staging subnet. Immediate symptom: error rate dropped from ~2.5% to ~0.1% and background syncs recovered.

Vendor confirmed they saw SYN-ACKs arrive at their edge and that the reverse path was being re-translated in our cluster prior to the fixes. We’ll keep the temporary mitigations in place until we can roll the long-term fix (consistent-hash SNAT) next week.

Please add the following items to the postmortem/action list:
- Permanent SNAT consistent-hash rollout (owner: Karthik)
- PMTU validation across GRE/VXLAN (owner: Marissa)
- Add a canary test that exercises outbound flows following SNAT pool rotations (owner: Kim)
- Update runbook and include tcpdump & conntrack snapshot checklist (owner: Marissa)

If you want I can keep the war-room notes in a Drive folder and share. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

—Tomek
